memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Know therefore that the Lord your God is God; he is the faithful God, keeping his covenant of love to a thousand generations of those who love him and keep his commandments. But those who hate him he will repay to their face by destruction; he will not be slow to repay to their face those who hate him. - Deut 7:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Moses calls Israel to "know" something deep and steadying: the Lord is "the faithful God." He keeps His covenant of love to a thousand generations. When God makes a promise, He keeps it — not for a while, not until it becomes inconvenient, but faithfully, across the ages. His love is not fickle or fragile. It is a committed, covenant love that endures far beyond our ability to imagine.

Notice the beautiful imbalance again: His steadfast love reaches "a thousand generations," while His judgment falls on those who persist in hating Him. God is overflowing with faithful love, and His justice, though real and serious, is never disconnected from His character. He is both perfectly loving and perfectly just — and we need Him to be both. A God who ignored evil would not be good; a God without mercy would leave us hopeless.

The wonder of the gospel is that God's faithfulness and His justice meet perfectly at the cross. There, God did not simply overlook our sin, nor did He abandon us to judgment. Instead, His own Son bore the judgment so that His covenant love could reach us. "If we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he cannot disown himself" (2 Tim 2:13). Whatever you are facing, you can build your life on this: God is the faithful God. He keeps His promises. His love holds.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do I truly trust that God is faithful to keep His promises?
- How do I hold together God's steadfast love and His justice?
- Where do I need to rest on God's faithfulness today?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Faithful God, You keep Your covenant of love across a thousand generations, and You are both perfectly loving and perfectly just. Thank You that Your faithfulness and justice met at the cross for me. Help me build my life on Your unfailing promises. Amen.
